title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)


EPILOGUE

That is what the Blessed One said when dwelling among the Magadhans at the Pāsāṇaka shrine. Asked in turn by the sixteen brahmans, he answered their questions. And if one were to practice the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, knowing the meaning and Dhamma of each of these questions, one would go to the far shore of birth & death. Because these Dhammas lead there, this Dhamma-sequence is called 'To the Far Shore.'

Ajita, Tissa-metteyya,

Puṇṇaka & Mettagū,

Dhotaka & Upasīva,

Nanda & Hemaka,

Todeyya & Kappa,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
Dhotaka & Upasīva,

Nanda & Hemaka,

Todeyya & Kappa,

the wise Jatukaṇṇin,

Bhadrāvudha & Udaya,

Posāla the brahman,

Mogharāja the intelligent,

and Piṅgiya the great seer:

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
Posāla the brahman,

Mogharāja the intelligent,

and Piṅgiya the great seer:

They went to the Awakened One,

consummate in conduct, the seer.

They went to the excellent Awakened One,

asking subtle questions.

The Awakened One,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
They went to the excellent Awakened One,

asking subtle questions.

The Awakened One,

when asked their questions,

answered in line with the truth.

By answering their questions, the sage

delighted the brahmans.

They, delighted by the One with Eyes—

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
By answering their questions, the sage

delighted the brahmans.

They, delighted by the One with Eyes—

Awakened, Kinsman of the Sun—

lived the holy life

in the presence of the one

of foremost discernment.

Whoever would practice

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
in the presence of the one

of foremost discernment.

Whoever would practice

as the Awakened One taught

concerning each of these questions,

would go from the near shore to the far—

would go from the near shore to the far

developing the path supreme.

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
would go from the near shore to the far—

would go from the near shore to the far

developing the path supreme.

The path is for going beyond,

and so it's called 'To the Far Shore.'

Venerable Piṅgiya:

'I will recite 'To the Far Shore.'

As he saw, so he taught—

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
Venerable Piṅgiya:

'I will recite 'To the Far Shore.'

As he saw, so he taught—

stainless, of deep intelligence,

the Nāga with

no sensuality,

no forest:

For what reason would he tell a lie?

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
no sensuality,

no forest:

For what reason would he tell a lie?

His delusion & stains

left behind; left behind,

his hypocrisy, conceit:

Let me praise his beautiful words.

He who is truly described

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
his hypocrisy, conceit:

Let me praise his beautiful words.

He who is truly described

as

dispeller of darkness,

awakened,

All-around Eye,

gone to the end of the cosmos,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
awakened,

All-around Eye,

gone to the end of the cosmos,

all his becoming transcended,

effluent-free,

his stress all abandoned:

He is served by me.

As a bird leaving a scrubby grove

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
his stress all abandoned:

He is served by me.

As a bird leaving a scrubby grove

would dwell in a forest abundant in fruit,

even so, I have left those of next-to-no vision,

have arrived

like a swan at a large lake.

In the past,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
have arrived

like a swan at a large lake.

In the past,

before hearing Gotama's message,

when anyone explained 'It is,' 'It will be,'

all that was hearsay,

quotation marks.

All that promoted conjecture

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
all that was hearsay,

quotation marks.

All that promoted conjecture

and gave me no pleasure.

Sitting alone—

the dispeller of darkness,

shining, bringer of light,

Gotama of deep knowledge,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
the dispeller of darkness,

shining, bringer of light,

Gotama of deep knowledge,

Gotama of deep intelligence:

He taught me the Dhamma

timeless, visible here-&-now,

the ending of craving,

calamity-free,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
timeless, visible here-&-now,

the ending of craving,

calamity-free,

whose likeness is nowhere at all.'

Bāvarī:

'Piṅgiya, for even a moment

can you stay apart from him—

Gotama of deep knowledge,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
'Piṅgiya, for even a moment

can you stay apart from him—

Gotama of deep knowledge,

Gotama of deep intelligence,

who taught you the Dhamma

timeless, visible here-&-now,

the ending of craving,

calamity-free,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
timeless, visible here-&-now,

the ending of craving,

calamity-free,

whose likeness is nowhere at all?'

Venerable Piṅgiya:

'No, brahman, not even for a moment

can I stay apart from him—

Gotama of deep knowledge,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
'No, brahman, not even for a moment

can I stay apart from him—

Gotama of deep knowledge,

Gotama of deep intelligence,

who taught me the Dhamma

timeless, visible here-&-now,

the ending of craving,

calamity-free,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
timeless, visible here-&-now,

the ending of craving,

calamity-free,

whose likeness is nowhere at all.

I see him with my heart

as if with my eye—

heedful, brahman, by day & by night.

I spend the night paying homage to him,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
as if with my eye—

heedful, brahman, by day & by night.

I spend the night paying homage to him,

and that way, as it were,

not staying apart.

My conviction, rapture,

mindfulness, & heart,

don't stray from Gotama's message.

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
My conviction, rapture,

mindfulness, & heart,

don't stray from Gotama's message.

To whatever direction he goes,

the one deeply discerning,

to that direction I bow down.

I am old, my stamina frail,

which is why my body doesn't run away to there.

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
to that direction I bow down.

I am old, my stamina frail,

which is why my body doesn't run away to there.

But through the machine of my resolves

I constantly go,

for my heart, brahman, is connected to him.

Floundering in the mud,

I swam from island to island,

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
for my heart, brahman, is connected to him.

Floundering in the mud,

I swam from island to island,

but then I saw the One Self-Awakened,

crossed over the flood, effluent-free.

'As Vakkali has shown his conviction—

as Bhadrāvudha & Āḷavi Gotama too—

so will you show your conviction, Piṅgiya.

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
'As Vakkali has shown his conviction—

as Bhadrāvudha & Āḷavi Gotama too—

so will you show your conviction, Piṅgiya.

You will go beyond the realm of death.'

I feel confidence all the more,

having heard the words of the sage,

his roof opened-up, self-awakened,

quick-witted, free from rigidity.

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
having heard the words of the sage,

his roof opened-up, self-awakened,

quick-witted, free from rigidity.

Knowing the supreme devas,

he knows all dhammas, from high to low:

the Teacher who puts an end

to the questions

of those admitting

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
the Teacher who puts an end

to the questions

of those admitting

their doubt.

To the untaken-in, unshaken,

whose likeness is nowhere at all:

Yes, I will go there.

I've no doubt about that.

title: SUTTA NIPĀTA 5. : THE TO-THE-FAR-SHORE CHAPTER  (PĀRĀYANA VAGGA)
text:
whose likeness is nowhere at all:

Yes, I will go there.

I've no doubt about that.

Remember me thus

as one whose mind

is decided.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:1  SUBHŪTI
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:1  SUBHŪTI

My hut is roofed, comfortable,

free of drafts;

my mind, well-centered,

released.

I remain ardent.

So, rain-deva.

Go ahead & rain.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:2  MAHĀ KOṬṬHITA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:2  MAHĀ KOṬṬHITA

Calmed, restrained,

giving counsel unruffled,

he shakes off evil qualities—

as the breeze,

a leaf from a tree.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:3  KAṄKHĀ (DOUBTING) REVATA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:3  KAṄKHĀ (DOUBTING) REVATA

See this:

the discernment

of the Tathāgatas,

like a fire ablaze in the night,

giving light, giving eyes,

to those who come,

subduing their doubt.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:6  DABBA ('CAPABLE')
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:6  DABBA ('CAPABLE')

Whoever,

hard to tame,

has been tamed by taming,

—capable, contented,

crossed over doubt,

victorious, as his fears

are dispersed:

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:6  DABBA ('CAPABLE')
text:
crossed over doubt,

victorious, as his fears

are dispersed:

He is capable,

unbound,

steadfast in mind.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:7  BHALLIYA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:7  BHALLIYA

Who scatters the troops

of the King of Death—

as a great flood,

a very weak bridge made of reeds—

is victorious,

for his fears are dispersed.

He's tamed,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:7  BHALLIYA
text:
is victorious,

for his fears are dispersed.

He's tamed,

unbound,

steadfast in mind.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:10  PUṆṆAMĀSA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:10  PUṆṆAMĀSA

Whoever,

a master of knowing,

contented,

restrained in mind,

destroys longing for here & beyond,

unsmeared with regard to all dhammas,

would know the arising-&-disbanding

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:10  PUṆṆAMĀSA
text:
destroys longing for here & beyond,

unsmeared with regard to all dhammas,

would know the arising-&-disbanding

of the world.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:13  VANAVACCHA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:13  VANAVACCHA

The color of blue-dark clouds,

glistening,

cooled with the waters

of clear-flowing streams

covered with ladybugs:

Those rocky crags

refresh me.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:14  VANAVACCHA'S PUPIL
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:14  VANAVACCHA'S PUPIL

My preceptor said to me:

Let's go from here, Sīvaka.

My body stays in the village;

my mind has gone to the wilds.

Even though lying down,

I go.

There's no tying down

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:14  VANAVACCHA'S PUPIL
text:
Even though lying down,

I go.

There's no tying down

one who knows.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:16  BELAṬṬHASĪSA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:16  BELAṬṬHASĪSA

Just as a fine thoroughbred steed,

with swishing tail & mane

runs with next-to-no effort,

so my days & nights

run with next-to-no effort

now that I've gained a pleasure

not of the flesh.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:18  SIṄGĀLAPITAR
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:18  SIṄGĀLAPITAR

There was an heir to the One Awakened,

a monk in the Bhesakaḷā forest,

who suffused this whole earth

with the perception of

'bones.'

Quickly, I'd say, he abandoned

sensual passion.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:21  NIGRODHA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:21  NIGRODHA

I'm not afraid

of danger,

of fear.

Our Teacher's adept

in the deathless.

Where danger, where fear

do not remain:

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:21  NIGRODHA
text:
in the deathless.

Where danger, where fear

do not remain:

That's the path

by which the monks go.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:22  CITTAKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:22  CITTAKA

Peacocks,

crested, blue, with gorgeous necks,

cry out

in the Kāraṁvī woods,

thrilled by the cold wind.

They awaken the sleeper

to meditate.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:23  GOSĀLA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:23  GOSĀLA

I—having eaten honey-rice

in a bamboo patch

and rightly grasping the aggregates'

arising-disbanding—

will return to the hillside, intent

on seclusion.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:25  NANDIYA (TO MĀRA)
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:25  NANDIYA (TO MĀRA)

Like splendor, his mind,

continually fruitful:

Attack a monk like that,

you Dark One,

and you'll fall

into pain.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:26  ABHAYA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:26  ABHAYA

Hearing the well-spoken words

of the Awakened One,

Kinsman of the Sun,

I pierced what is subtle—

as if, with an arrow,

the tip of a horse-tail hair.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:29  HĀRITA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:29  HĀRITA

Hārita,

raise yourself up-

right

and, straightening your mind

—like a fletcher, an arrow—

shatter ignorance

to bits.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:31  GAHURATĪRIYA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:31  GAHURATĪRIYA

Touched by gnats & mosquitoes,

in the wilds, the great forest,

like a nāga elephant

at the head of a battle,

mindful,

he acquiesces to that.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:32  SUPPIYA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:32  SUPPIYA

I'll make a trade:

aging for the ageless,

burning for the unbound—

the highest peace,

the unexcelled rest

from the yoke.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:33  SOPĀKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:33  SOPĀKA

Just as one would be good

to one's dear only child,

one should be good to all creatures

everywhere.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:39  TISSA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:39  TISSA

As if struck by a sword,

as if his head were on fire,

a monk should live the wandering life

—mindful—

for the abandoning of sensual passion.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:41  SIRIVAḌḌHA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:41  SIRIVAḌḌHA

Lightning lands on the cleft

between Vebhāra & Paṇḍava,

but,

having gone to the cleft in the mountains,

he's absorbed in jhāna—the son

of the one without compare,

the one who is Such.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:43  SUMAṄGALA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:43  SUMAṄGALA

So freed! So freed!

So thoroughly freed am I

from three crooked things:

my sickles, my shovels, my plows.

Even if they were here,

right here,

I'd be done with them,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:43  SUMAṄGALA
text:
Even if they were here,

right here,

I'd be done with them,

done.

Do jhāna, Sumaṅgala.

Do jhāna, Sumaṅgala.

Sumaṅgala, stay heedful.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:49  RĀMAṆEYYAKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:49  RĀMAṆEYYAKA

Even with all the whistles & whistling,

the calls of the birds,

this, my mind, doesn't waver,

for my delight is in

oneness.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:50  VIMALA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:50  VIMALA

The earth's sprinkled

with rain, wind

is blowing, lightning

wanders the sky,

but my thoughts are stilled,

well-centered

my mind.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:56  KUṬIVIHĀRIN (1)
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:56  KUṬIVIHĀRIN (1)

Who's in the hut?

A monk's in the hut—

free from passion,

with well-centered mind.

Know this, my friend:

The hut you built

wasn't wasted.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:57  KUṬIVIHĀRIN (2)
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:57  KUṬIVIHĀRIN (2)

This was your old hut,

and you aspire to another,

new hut.

Discard your hope for a hut, monk.

A new hut will be

painful all over again.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:61  VAPPA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:61  VAPPA

One who sees

sees who sees,

sees who doesn't.

One who doesn't see

doesn't

see who sees

or who doesn't.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:68  EKUDĀNIYA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:68  EKUDĀNIYA

Of heightened awareness & heedful,

the sage trained in sagacity's ways:

He has no sorrows, one who is Such,

calmed & ever mindful.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:73  MĀṆAVA
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:73  MĀṆAVA
text:
a person dead, gone to life's end,

I left

for the life gone forth,

abandoning the sensuality

that entices the heart.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:75  SUSĀRADA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:75  SUSĀRADA

Good the sight

of the well-rectified:

Doubt is cut off,

intelligence grows.

Even fools

they make wise—

so the company of the true

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:75  SUSĀRADA
text:
Even fools

they make wise—

so the company of the true

is good.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:84  NĪTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:84  NĪTA

Asleep the whole night,

delighting in company by day:

When, when

will the fool

bring suffering & stress

to an end?

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:85  SUNĀGA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:85  SUNĀGA

Adept in a theme for the mind,

sensing the savor of solitude,

practicing jhāna,

masterful, mindful,

you'd attain a pleasure

not of the flesh.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:86  NĀGITA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:86  NĀGITA

Outside of this path,

the path of the many

who teach other things

doesn't go to unbinding

as does this:

Thus the Blessed One

instructs the Saṅgha,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:86  NĀGITA
text:
as does this:

Thus the Blessed One

instructs the Saṅgha,

truly showing the palms of his hands.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:88  AJJUNA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:88  AJJUNA

Able was I

to raise myself from water

to dry land.

Swept along by the great flood,

I penetrated

the truths.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:93  ERAKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:93  ERAKA

Sensual pleasures are stressful,

Eraka.

Sensual pleasures aren't ease.

Whoever loves sensual pleasures

loves stress,     Eraka.

Whoever doesn't,

doesn't love stress.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:95  CAKKHUPĀLA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:95  CAKKHUPĀLA

I'm blind,

my eyes are destroyed.

I've stumbled

on a wilderness track.

Even

if I must crawl,

I'll go on,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:95  CAKKHUPĀLA
text:
Even

if I must crawl,

I'll go on,

but not with an evil companion.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:100  DEVASABHA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:100  DEVASABHA

Consummate in the right exertions,

the establishings of mindfulness his range,

blanketed with the flowers of release,

he will, without effluent, totally unbind.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:101  BELAṬṬHKĀNI
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:101  BELAṬṬHKĀNI

Abandoning the householder's state,

but with no mastery,

lazy, gluttonous,

using his mouth as a plough

like a great hog fattened on fodder:

Again & again

he goes to the womb—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:101  BELAṬṬHKĀNI
text:
like a great hog fattened on fodder:

Again & again

he goes to the womb—

the dullard.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:104  KHITAKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:104  KHITAKA

How light my body!

Touched by abundant

rapture & bliss,

—like a cotton tuft

borne on the breeze—

it seems to be floating

—my body!

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:109  SAṄGHARAKKHITA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:109  SAṄGHARAKKHITA

Why,

having gone into solitude,

does he not take account

of the message

of the one sympathetic

to his foremost well-being?

Because he dwells

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:109  SAṄGHARAKKHITA
text:
of the one sympathetic

to his foremost well-being?

Because he dwells

with his faculties

exposed,

like a tender deer

in the forest.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:110  USABHA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:110  USABHA

Trees on the hilltops

are flourishing,

watered by a new high-rising cloud,

giving birth to even more goodness

for Usabha—

desiring seclusion,

conscious of

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:110  USABHA
text:
for Usabha—

desiring seclusion,

conscious of

'wilderness.'

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:111  JENTA
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:111  JENTA
text:
it's hard to keep going

with whatever we get:

So it's right that we ponder

continually

continual

inconstancy.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:113  VANAVACCHA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:113  VANAVACCHA

With clear waters &

massive boulders,

frequented by monkeys &

deer,

covered with moss &

water weeds:

Those rocky crags refresh me.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:114  ADHIMUTTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:114  ADHIMUTTA

For one heavy

with bodily offenses,

greedy

for carcass pleasures

while life is wasting away:

From where will there come

contemplative-excellence?

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:118  KIMBILA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:118  KIMBILA

As if sent by a curse,

it drops on us—

aging.

The body seems     other,

though it's still the same one.

I'm still here

& have never been absent from it,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:118  KIMBILA
text:
though it's still the same one.

I'm still here

& have never been absent from it,

but I remember myself

as if somebody else's.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:119  VAJJIPUTTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:119  VAJJIPUTTA

Coming to the bower

at the root of a tree,

placing

unbinding

in your heart,

do jhāna, Gotama,

& don't be heedless.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:119  VAJJIPUTTA
text:
in your heart,

do jhāna, Gotama,

& don't be heedless.

What use is this

chitter-chatter

to you?

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:120  ISIDATTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 1:120  ISIDATTA

The five aggregates,

having been comprehended,

stand with their root

cut through.

For me

the ending of stress

is reached;

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 1:120  ISIDATTA
text:
For me

the ending of stress

is reached;

the ending of effluents,

attained.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:3  VALLIYA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:3  VALLIYA

A monkey,

coming to the little hut

with five doors,

goes from door to door, knocking

moment by moment.

Stand still, monkey,

don't run.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:3  VALLIYA
text:
moment by moment.

Stand still, monkey,

don't run.

It's not yours

as it was before.

You're bound by discernment.

You won't get far away.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:9  GOTAMA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:9  GOTAMA

At ease sleep the sages

who

are not bound to women,

in whom

always to be protected

is the truth

very hard to gain.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:9  GOTAMA
text:
always to be protected

is the truth

very hard to gain.

Sensuality,

we've carried out

your execution.

No longer are we in your debt.

We go now to unbinding

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:9  GOTAMA
text:
your execution.

No longer are we in your debt.

We go now to unbinding

where,

having gone,

one doesn't

grieve.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:11  MAHĀ CUNDA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:11  MAHĀ CUNDA

Listening well increases learning.

What is learned increases discernment.

Through discernment one knows the goal.

When known, the goal brings bliss.

Stay in isolated lodgings;

live for freedom from fetters.

If you don't attain delight there,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:11  MAHĀ CUNDA
text:
Stay in isolated lodgings;

live for freedom from fetters.

If you don't attain delight there,

then live in the Saṅgha,

your mind protected,

mindful.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:13  HERAÑÑAKĀNI
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:13  HERAÑÑAKĀNI

Days & nights

fly past.

Life

comes to an end.

The span of mortals

runs out,

like the water of a piddling stream.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:13  HERAÑÑAKĀNI
text:
The span of mortals

runs out,

like the water of a piddling stream.

But the fool doing evil deeds

doesn't realize that later

it's bitter for him:

evil for him

the result.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:16  MAHĀKĀLA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:16  MAHĀKĀLA

This swarthy woman

[preparing a corpse for cremation]

—crow-like, enormous—

breaking a thigh & then the other

thigh,

breaking an arm & then the other

arm,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:16  MAHĀKĀLA
text:
thigh,

breaking an arm & then the other

arm,

cracking open the head,

like a pot of curds,

she sits with them heaped up beside her.

Whoever, unknowing,

makes acquisitions

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:16  MAHĀKĀLA
text:
she sits with them heaped up beside her.

Whoever, unknowing,

makes acquisitions

—the fool—

returns over & over

to suffering & stress.

So, discerning,

don't make acquisitions.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:16  MAHĀKĀLA
text:
to suffering & stress.

So, discerning,

don't make acquisitions.

May I never lie

with my head cracked open

again.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:17  TISSA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:17  TISSA

He gains many enemies,
 one who—shaven-headed,
 wearing an outer robe—
gains food, drink, cloth, lodgings.


Knowing this drawback,
this great danger in honors,
a monk, gaining little,
not soggy,
should go forth
 mindfully.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:19  NANDA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:19  NANDA

From inappropriate attention
I was devoted to ornament,
 restless & vain,
driven by sensual passion.


With the help of the Buddha,
the Kinsman of the Sun,
skilled in strategies,
I, practicing appropriately,
 plucked my mind
out of becoming.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:24  VALLIYA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:24  VALLIYA

What needs to be done

with firm persistence,

what needs to be done

by one who hopes for awakening,

that I will do.

I will not fail.

See: persistence & striving!

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:24  VALLIYA
text:
that I will do.

I will not fail.

See: persistence & striving!

You show me the path:

the straight,

the plunge into deathlessness.

I, through sagacity,

will reach it, know it,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:24  VALLIYA
text:
the plunge into deathlessness.

I, through sagacity,

will reach it, know it,

as the stream of the Ganges,

the sea.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:26  PUṆṆAMĀSA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:26  PUṆṆAMĀSA

Shedding five hindrances

to reach rest from the yoke,

taking the Dhamma as mirror

my own knowledge & vision,

I reflected on this body—

the whole thing,

inside & out,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:26  PUṆṆAMĀSA
text:
I reflected on this body—

the whole thing,

inside & out,

my own & others'.

How vain & empty the body appeared!

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:27  NANDAKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:27  NANDAKA

Just as a fine thoroughbred steed

stumbling, regains its stance,

feeling all the more urgency,

& draws its burden

undaunted.

In the same way, remember me:

consummate in vision,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:27  NANDAKA
text:
undaunted.

In the same way, remember me:

consummate in vision,

a disciple of the Rightly

Self-awakened One,

the Awakened One's thoroughbred child,

his son.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:30  KAṆHADINNA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:30  KAṆHADINNA

Men of integrity

have been attended to,

the Dhamma repeatedly

listened to.

Having listened,

I followed the straight way,

the plunge into deathlessness.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:30  KAṆHADINNA
text:
Having listened,

I followed the straight way,

the plunge into deathlessness.

Passion for becoming,

having been killed by me,

no further such passion

is found in me.

It neither was

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:30  KAṆHADINNA
text:
no further such passion

is found in me.

It neither was

nor will be

nor is found in me

even now.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:32  SIVAKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:32  SIVAKA

Inconstant little houses:

now here,

now there,       again

& again,

I sought the house-builder.

Painful is birth, again

& again.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:32  SIVAKA
text:
I sought the house-builder.

Painful is birth, again

& again.

House-builder, you're seen!

You will not build a house again.

All your rafters are broken,

and your gables torn down.

Released from restriction, the mind

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:32  SIVAKA
text:
All your rafters are broken,

and your gables torn down.

Released from restriction, the mind

will

be blown out

right here.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:36  KHITAKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:36  KHITAKA

Whose mind, standing like rock,

doesn't shake,

dispassionate for things that spark passion,

unprovoked by things that spark provocation?

When one's mind is developed like this,

from where can there come to him

suffering & stress?

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:36  KHITAKA
text:
When one's mind is developed like this,

from where can there come to him

suffering & stress?

My mind, standing like rock,

doesn't shake,

dispassionate for things that spark passion,

unprovoked by things that spark provocation.

When my mind is developed like this,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:36  KHITAKA
text:
dispassionate for things that spark passion,

unprovoked by things that spark provocation.

When my mind is developed like this,

from where can there come to me

suffering & stress?

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:37  SOṆA POṬIRIYAPUTTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:37  SOṆA POṬIRIYAPUTTA

It's not for sleeping,

the night garlanded

with zodiac stars.

The night, for one who knows,

is for staying awake.

If I were to fall from my elephant's shoulder,

and a tusker trampled me,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:37  SOṆA POṬIRIYAPUTTA
text:
is for staying awake.

If I were to fall from my elephant's shoulder,

and a tusker trampled me,

death in battle would be better for me,

than that I, defeated,

survive.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:42  DHAMMAPĀLA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:42  DHAMMAPĀLA

The young monk
devoted to the Buddha's message,
is wakeful among those who sleep.
 His life is not in vain.


So, intelligent,
one should commit oneself
to conviction & virtue,
confidence & Dhamma-vision,
 remembering the Buddhas' message.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:43  BRAHMĀLI
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:43  BRAHMĀLI

Whose faculties have been made tranquil,
like horses well-tamed by a charioteer —
effluents abandoned,
envied even by devas,
 Such?


My faculties have been made tranquil
like horses well-tamed by a charioteer —
effluents abandoned,
I'm envied even by devas.
 Such.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:47  ANŪPAMA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 2:47  ANŪPAMA

Coming into the conceit of delight, the mind

impales itself on a stake.

Wherever's a stake, a chopping block,

there, only there, you turn.

You, mind, I call an unlucky die.

You, I call a mind-traitor.

You've gained a Teacher hard to gain.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 2:47  ANŪPAMA
text:
You, mind, I call an unlucky die.

You, I call a mind-traitor.

You've gained a Teacher hard to gain.

Don't urge me on to my loss.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:5  MĀTAṄGAPUTTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 3:5  MĀTAṄGAPUTTA

It's too cold,

too hot,

too late in the evening—

people who say this,

shirking their work:

The moment passes them by.

Whoever regards cold & heat

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:5  MĀTAṄGAPUTTA
text:
shirking their work:

The moment passes them by.

Whoever regards cold & heat

as no more than grass,

doing his manly duties,

won't fall away

from ease.

With my chest

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:5  MĀTAṄGAPUTTA
text:
won't fall away

from ease.

With my chest

I push through wild grasses—

spear-grass,

ribbon-grass,

rushes—

cultivating a heart

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:5  MĀTAṄGAPUTTA
text:
ribbon-grass,

rushes—

cultivating a heart

bent on seclusion.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:8  YASOJA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 3:8  YASOJA

His limbs knotted

like a kālā plant,

his body lean

& lined with veins,

knowing moderation

in food & drink:

the man of undaunted heart.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:8  YASOJA
text:
knowing moderation

in food & drink:

the man of undaunted heart.

Touched by gnats

& horseflies

in the wilds,

the great wood,

like an elephant

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:8  YASOJA
text:
in the wilds,

the great wood,

like an elephant

at the head of a battle:

He, mindful,

should stay there,

endure.

One alone is like Brahmā,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:8  YASOJA
text:
should stay there,

endure.

One alone is like Brahmā,

two, like devas,

three, like a village,

more than that:

a hullabaloo.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:9  SATIMATTIYA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 3:9  SATIMATTIYA

Before, you had faith.
Today you don't.
What is yours
is just for you.
I've done nothing wrong.


For I've seen that faith is inconstant,
 wavering.
Even they who are passionate
 lose their passion.
Why should a sage waste away over that?

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:9  SATIMATTIYA
text:
wavering.
Even they who are passionate
 lose their passion.
Why should a sage waste away over that?


A sage's meal is cooked
little by little, in this family and that.
I will go for alms.
I have the strength of my legs.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:13  ABHIBHŪTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 3:13  ABHIBHŪTA

Listen, kinsmen, all of you,

as many as are assembled here.

I will teach you the Dhamma:

Painful is birth,

again & again.

Rouse yourselves.

Go forth.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:13  ABHIBHŪTA
text:
again & again.

Rouse yourselves.

Go forth.

Apply yourselves

to the Awakened One's bidding.

Scatter the army of Death

as an elephant would

a shed made of reeds.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:13  ABHIBHŪTA
text:
Scatter the army of Death

as an elephant would

a shed made of reeds.

He who,

in this Dhamma & Vinaya,

stays heedful,

abandoning birth,

the wandering-on,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:13  ABHIBHŪTA
text:
stays heedful,

abandoning birth,

the wandering-on,

will put an end

to suffering & stress.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:14  GOTAMA
THERAGĀTHĀ 3:14  GOTAMA
THERAGĀTHĀ 3:14  GOTAMA
text:
from time to time;

settled in the elements of form,

the elements of formlessness,

neither perception, perception-less.

Ways of taking birth

are now known:

devoid of essence,

unstable,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:14  GOTAMA
text:
are now known:

devoid of essence,

unstable,

conditioned,

always blown along.

Knowing them

as born from my self,

mindful

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:14  GOTAMA
text:
Knowing them

as born from my self,

mindful

I went right to peace.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:15  HĀRITA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 3:15  HĀRITA

Whoever wants to do later

what he should have done first,

falls away from the easeful state

& later repents.

One should speak

as one would act,

& not

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:15  HĀRITA
text:
One should speak

as one would act,

& not

as one wouldn't.

When one speaks without acting,

the wise, they can tell.

How very easeful:

unbinding,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:15  HĀRITA
text:
the wise, they can tell.

How very easeful:

unbinding,

as taught by the Rightly

Self-awakened One—

sorrowless,

dustless,

secure,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 3:15  HĀRITA
text:
sorrowless,

dustless,

secure,

where stress

& suffering

cease.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:2  BHAGU
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 4:2  BHAGU

I, overcome with torpor,
left my dwelling.
Stepping up on the walking path,
 I fell on the ground
 right there.
Rubbing my limbs,
I got up on the path again.
Walking back & forth on the path,
I became well-centered within.
Apt attention arose in me,
 the drawbacks appeared,
  disenchantment stood
  at an even keel:

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:2  BHAGU
text:
I became well-centered within.
Apt attention arose in me,
 the drawbacks appeared,
  disenchantment stood
  at an even keel:


With that, my heart was released.


See the Dhamma's true rightness!
The three knowledges
have been attained;
the Buddha's bidding,
 done.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:4  NANDAKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 4:4  NANDAKA

A curse on bodies—
full of foul smells,
siding with Māra,
   oozing,
where nine streams are always flowing.


Don't think much of them,
Don't offend the Tathāgatas,
who don't delight even in heaven,
to say nothing of the human realm.


But fools of little intelligence,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:4  NANDAKA
text:
Don't offend the Tathāgatas,
who don't delight even in heaven,
to say nothing of the human realm.


But fools of little intelligence,
with bad advisers,
cloaked in delusion:
Those sorts of people delight there
in the snare that Māra's thrown down.


Whereas those dispassionate for
 passion,
 aversion,
 ignorance

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:4  NANDAKA
text:
Whereas those dispassionate for
 passion,
 aversion,
 ignorance
don't delight there,
have cut the cord,
   unsnared.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:8  RĀHULA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 4:8  RĀHULA

In both ways

consummate,

I'm known as Rāhula

the Fortunate:

because     I'm the son of the Buddha,

because     I've the eye that sees Dhammas,

because     my effluents are ended,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:8  RĀHULA
text:
because     I'm the son of the Buddha,

because     I've the eye that sees Dhammas,

because     my effluents are ended,

because     I've no further becoming.

I'm deserving of offerings,

a worthy one

a three-knowledge man,

one with sight

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:8  RĀHULA
text:
a worthy one

a three-knowledge man,

one with sight

of the deathless.

Those

blinded       by sensuality

covered       by the net,

veiled       by the veil of craving,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:8  RĀHULA
text:
blinded       by sensuality

covered       by the net,

veiled       by the veil of craving,

bound       by the Kinsman of the heedless,

are like fish in the mouth of a trap.

Throwing that sensuality aside,

cutting through Māra's bond,

pulling out craving, root & all,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:8  RĀHULA
text:
Throwing that sensuality aside,

cutting through Māra's bond,

pulling out craving, root & all,

cooled am I.

Unbound.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:10  DHAMMIKA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 4:10  DHAMMIKA

The Dhamma protects

those who live by the Dhamma.

The Dhamma well-practiced

brings bliss.

This—the reward

when the Dhamma's well-practiced:

One who lives by the Dhamma

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:10  DHAMMIKA
text:
This—the reward

when the Dhamma's well-practiced:

One who lives by the Dhamma

doesn't go to a bad destination.

For Dhamma and non-

don't bear equal results.

Non-Dhamma leads you to hell;

Dhamma, to a good destination.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:10  DHAMMIKA
text:
don't bear equal results.

Non-Dhamma leads you to hell;

Dhamma, to a good destination.

So you should engender desire

for acts of Dhamma,

rejoicing

in the One     Well-Gone,

the one      who is Such.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:10  DHAMMIKA
text:
rejoicing

in the One     Well-Gone,

the one      who is Such.

Standing firm in the Dhamma,

of the foremost

One Well-Gone,

his disciples are guided

—enlightened—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:10  DHAMMIKA
text:
One Well-Gone,

his disciples are guided

—enlightened—

to the foremost

refuge supreme.

Burst       is the root of the boil;

the net of craving     uprooted.

He, having ended his wandering-on,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 4:10  DHAMMIKA
text:
Burst       is the root of the boil;

the net of craving     uprooted.

He, having ended his wandering-on,

has no stain—

like the moon

on a clear full-moon night.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:1  RĀJADATTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 5:1  RĀJADATTA

I, a monk,

gone to the charnel ground,

saw a woman cast away,

discarded

there in the cemetery.

Though some were disgusted,

seeing her—dead, evil—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:1  RĀJADATTA
text:
there in the cemetery.

Though some were disgusted,

seeing her—dead, evil—

lust

appeared,

as if I were blind

to the oozings.

In less time than it takes

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:1  RĀJADATTA
text:
as if I were blind

to the oozings.

In less time than it takes

for rice to cook,

I got out of that place.

Mindful, alert, I

sat down to one side.

Then apt attention arose in me,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:1  RĀJADATTA
text:
Mindful, alert, I

sat down to one side.

Then apt attention arose in me,

the drawbacks appeared,

disenchantment stood

at an even keel:

With that, my heart was released.

See the Dhamma's true rightness!

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:1  RĀJADATTA
text:
at an even keel:

With that, my heart was released.

See the Dhamma's true rightness!

The three knowledges

have been attained;

the Awakened One's bidding,

done.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:8  VAKKALI
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 5:8  VAKKALI

Stricken by sharp, wind-like pains,

you, monk, living in the forest grove

—harsh, with limited range for alms—

what, what will you do?

Suffusing my body

with abundant rapture & joy,

& enduring what's harsh,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:8  VAKKALI
text:
Suffusing my body

with abundant rapture & joy,

& enduring what's harsh,

I'll stay in the grove.

Developing the establishings of mindfulness,

strengths, faculties,

the factors for awakening,

I'll stay in the grove.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:8  VAKKALI
text:
strengths, faculties,

the factors for awakening,

I'll stay in the grove.

Reflecting on those who are resolute,

their persistence aroused,

constantly firm in their effort,

united in concord,

I'll stay in the grove.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:8  VAKKALI
text:
constantly firm in their effort,

united in concord,

I'll stay in the grove.

Recollecting the One Self-awakened,

self-tamed & centered,

untiring both day & night,

I'll stay

in the grove.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:10  YASADATTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 5:10  YASADATTA

Intent on quibbling,

the dullard hears the Conqueror's teaching.

He's as far from the True Dhamma

as the ground is from the sky.

Intent on quibbling,

the dullard hears the Conqueror's teaching.

He wanes from the True Dhamma

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:10  YASADATTA
text:
Intent on quibbling,

the dullard hears the Conqueror's teaching.

He wanes from the True Dhamma

like the moon in the dark half of the month.

Intent on quibbling,

the dullard hears the Conqueror's teaching.

He dries up in the True Dhamma

like a fish in next to no water.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:10  YASADATTA
text:
the dullard hears the Conqueror's teaching.

He dries up in the True Dhamma

like a fish in next to no water.

Intent on quibbling,

the dullard hears the Conqueror's teaching.

He doesn't grow in the True Dhamma,

like a rotten seed in a field.

But whoever hears the Conqueror's teaching

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:10  YASADATTA
text:
He doesn't grow in the True Dhamma,

like a rotten seed in a field.

But whoever hears the Conqueror's teaching

with guarded intent,

doing away with effluents

—all—

realizing the unshakable,

attaining the foremost peace,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 5:10  YASADATTA
text:
—all—

realizing the unshakable,

attaining the foremost peace,

—effluent-free—

totally unbinds.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:2  TEKICCHAKĀNI
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 6:2  TEKICCHAKĀNI

The grain: harvested.

The rice: gone to be threshed.

But I don't get any alms.

How will I get by?

Confident, recollect

the immeasurable Buddha.

Your body pervaded with rapture,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:2  TEKICCHAKĀNI
text:
Confident, recollect

the immeasurable Buddha.

Your body pervaded with rapture,

you'll be at the height

of continual joy.

Confident, recollect

the immeasurable Dhamma.

Your body pervaded with rapture,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:2  TEKICCHAKĀNI
text:
Confident, recollect

the immeasurable Dhamma.

Your body pervaded with rapture,

you'll be at the height

of continual joy.

Confident, recollect

the immeasurable Saṅgha.

Your body pervaded with rapture,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:2  TEKICCHAKĀNI
text:
Confident, recollect

the immeasurable Saṅgha.

Your body pervaded with rapture,

you'll be at the height

of continual joy.

You live in the open air.

Cold are these wintry nights.

Don't suffer, overcome with the cold.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:2  TEKICCHAKĀNI
text:
You live in the open air.

Cold are these wintry nights.

Don't suffer, overcome with the cold.

Go into your hut, with its fastened bolt.

I'll fasten the four

immeasurables.

With them, I'll dwell

in comfort.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:2  TEKICCHAKĀNI
text:
immeasurables.

With them, I'll dwell

in comfort.

I won't suffer from the cold,

dwelling

unperturbed.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:3  MAHĀNĀGA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 6:3  MAHĀNĀGA

One in whom respect for his fellows in the holy life

is not found,

wastes away from the True Dhamma

like a fish in next to no water.

One in whom respect for his fellows in the holy life

is not found,

doesn't grow in the True Dhamma,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:3  MAHĀNĀGA
text:
One in whom respect for his fellows in the holy life

is not found,

doesn't grow in the True Dhamma,

like a rotten seed in a field.

One in whom respect for his fellows in the holy life

is not found,

is far away from unbinding

in the teaching of the Dhamma king.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:3  MAHĀNĀGA
text:
is not found,

is far away from unbinding

in the teaching of the Dhamma king.

One in whom respect for his fellows in the holy life

is found,

doesn't waste away from the True Dhamma

like a fish in plentiful water.

One in whom respect for his fellows in the holy life

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:3  MAHĀNĀGA
text:
doesn't waste away from the True Dhamma

like a fish in plentiful water.

One in whom respect for his fellows in the holy life

is found,

grows in the True Dhamma,

like an excellent seed in a field.

One in whom respect for his fellows in the holy life

is found,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:3  MAHĀNĀGA
text:
like an excellent seed in a field.

One in whom respect for his fellows in the holy life

is found,

stands right in the presence of unbinding

in the teaching of the Dhamma king.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:5  MĀLUṄKYAPUTTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 6:5  MĀLUṄKYAPUTTA

When a person lives heedlessly,

his craving grows like a creeping vine.

He runs now here

& now      there,

as if looking for fruit:

a monkey in the forest.

If this sticky, uncouth craving

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:5  MĀLUṄKYAPUTTA
text:
as if looking for fruit:

a monkey in the forest.

If this sticky, uncouth craving

overcomes you in the world,

your sorrows grow like wild grass

after rain.

If, in the world, you overcome

this uncouth craving, hard to escape,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:5  MĀLUṄKYAPUTTA
text:
after rain.

If, in the world, you overcome

this uncouth craving, hard to escape,

sorrows roll off you,

like water beads off

a lotus.

To all of you gathered here

I say:

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:5  MĀLUṄKYAPUTTA
text:
a lotus.

To all of you gathered here

I say:

Good fortune.

Dig up craving

—as when seeking medicinal roots, wild grass—

by the root.

Don't let Māra cut you down

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:5  MĀLUṄKYAPUTTA
text:
—as when seeking medicinal roots, wild grass—

by the root.

Don't let Māra cut you down

—as a raging river, a reed—

over & over again.

Do what the Buddha says.

Don't let the moment pass by.

Those for whom the moment is past

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:5  MĀLUṄKYAPUTTA
text:
Do what the Buddha says.

Don't let the moment pass by.

Those for whom the moment is past

grieve, consigned to hell.

Heedlessness is dust.

Dust follows on heedlessness.

Through heedfulness, knowledge,

pull out

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:5  MĀLUṄKYAPUTTA
text:
Dust follows on heedlessness.

Through heedfulness, knowledge,

pull out

your own arrow

on your own.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:6  SAPPADĀSA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 6:6  SAPPADĀSA

Twenty five years since my going forth,

and no peace of awareness

—not a finger-snap's worth—

attained.

Having gained no oneness of mind,

I was wracked with lust.

Wailing, with my arms upheld,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:6  SAPPADĀSA
text:
Having gained no oneness of mind,

I was wracked with lust.

Wailing, with my arms upheld,

I ran amok from my dwelling—

'Or… or shall I take the knife?

What's the use of life to me?

If I were to renounce the training,

what sort of death would I have?'

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:6  SAPPADĀSA
text:
What's the use of life to me?

If I were to renounce the training,

what sort of death would I have?'

So, taking a razor,

I sat down on a bed.

And there was the razor,

placed ready to cut my own vein,

when apt attention arose in me,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:6  SAPPADĀSA
text:
And there was the razor,

placed ready to cut my own vein,

when apt attention arose in me,

the drawbacks appeared,

disenchantment stood

at an even keel:

With that, my heart was released.

See the Dhamma's true rightness!

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:6  SAPPADĀSA
text:
at an even keel:

With that, my heart was released.

See the Dhamma's true rightness!

The three knowledges

have been attained;

the Awakened One's bidding,

done.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:9  JENTA, THE ROYAL CHAPLAIN'S SON
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 6:9  JENTA, THE ROYAL CHAPLAIN'S SON

I was

drunk with the intoxication

of my birth, wealth, & sovereignty.

Drunk with the intoxication

of my body's build, coloring, & form,

I wandered about,

regarding no one

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:9  JENTA, THE ROYAL CHAPLAIN'S SON
text:
of my body's build, coloring, & form,

I wandered about,

regarding no one

as my equal or better.

Foolish, arrogant, haughty,

my banner held high.

I—disrespectful, arrogant, proud—

bowed down to no one,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:9  JENTA, THE ROYAL CHAPLAIN'S SON
text:
my banner held high.

I—disrespectful, arrogant, proud—

bowed down to no one,

not even

mother,

father,

or those commonly held

in respect.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:9  JENTA, THE ROYAL CHAPLAIN'S SON
text:
father,

or those commonly held

in respect.

Then—seeing the ultimate leader,

supreme, foremost of charioteers,

like a blazing sun,

arrayed with a squadron of monks—

casting away pride & intoxication

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:9  JENTA, THE ROYAL CHAPLAIN'S SON
text:
like a blazing sun,

arrayed with a squadron of monks—

casting away pride & intoxication

through an awareness serene & clear,

I bowed down

my

head

to him, supreme

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:9  JENTA, THE ROYAL CHAPLAIN'S SON
text:
my

head

to him, supreme

among all living beings.

Haughtiness & contempt

have been abandoned

—rooted out—

the conceit 'I am' is extracted,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:9  JENTA, THE ROYAL CHAPLAIN'S SON
text:
have been abandoned

—rooted out—

the conceit 'I am' is extracted,

all forms of pride, destroyed.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:10  SUMANA THE NOVICE
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 6:10  SUMANA THE NOVICE

When I was seven

& newly gone forth,

having conquered with my power

the great powerful serpent,

I was fetching water for my preceptor

from the great lake, Anotatta,

when the Teacher saw me & said:

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:10  SUMANA THE NOVICE
text:
I was fetching water for my preceptor

from the great lake, Anotatta,

when the Teacher saw me & said:

'Look, Sāriputta, at that one,

the young boy coming there,

carrying a pot of water,

well-centered within,

his practices—inspiring;

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:10  SUMANA THE NOVICE
text:
carrying a pot of water,

well-centered within,

his practices—inspiring;

his bearing—admirable.

He's Anuruddha's novice,

mature in his powers,

made thoroughbred by a thoroughbred,

good by one who is good,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:10  SUMANA THE NOVICE
text:
mature in his powers,

made thoroughbred by a thoroughbred,

good by one who is good,

tamed by Anuruddha,

trained by one whose task

is done.

He,     having reached the highest peace

& realized the unshakable,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:10  SUMANA THE NOVICE
text:
is done.

He,     having reached the highest peace

& realized the unshakable,

Sumana the novice

wants this:

'Don't let anyone know me.'

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:12  BRAHMADATTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 6:12  BRAHMADATTA

Whence is there anger

in one without anger

tamed, calmed, living in tune,

released through right knowing,

Such?

You make things worse

when you flare up

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:12  BRAHMADATTA
text:
Such?

You make things worse

when you flare up

at someone who's angry.

Whoever doesn't flare up

at someone who's angry

wins a battle

hard to win.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:12  BRAHMADATTA
text:
at someone who's angry

wins a battle

hard to win.

You live for the good of both

—your own, the other's—

when, knowing the other's provoked,

you mindfully grow calm.

When you work the cure of both

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:12  BRAHMADATTA
text:
when, knowing the other's provoked,

you mindfully grow calm.

When you work the cure of both

—your own, the other's—

those who think you a fool

know nothing of Dhamma.

If anger arises,

reflect on the saw simile.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:12  BRAHMADATTA
text:
know nothing of Dhamma.

If anger arises,

reflect on the saw simile.

If craving for savor,

remember the son's-flesh simile.

If your mind runs loose

after sensual pleasures

& states of becoming,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:12  BRAHMADATTA
text:
If your mind runs loose

after sensual pleasures

& states of becoming,

quickly restrain it with mindfulness

as you would a bad ox

eating grain.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:13  SIRIMAṆḌA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 6:13  SIRIMAṆḌA

Rain soddens what's covered

& doesn't sodden what's exposed.

So open up what's covered up,

so that it won't get soddened by the rain.

Attacked by death

is the world,

surrounded by aging,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:13  SIRIMAṆḌA
text:
Attacked by death

is the world,

surrounded by aging,

beset by the arrow of craving,

always obscured by desire.

Attacked by death

is the world,

& encircled by aging,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:13  SIRIMAṆḌA
text:
Attacked by death

is the world,

& encircled by aging,

constantly beaten, with no shelter,

like a thief

sentenced to punishment.

They encroach like masses of flame,

these three:

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:13  SIRIMAṆḌA
text:
sentenced to punishment.

They encroach like masses of flame,

these three:

death, aging, & illness.

There's no strength to confront them,

no speed to run away.

Make the day not-in-vain,

a little or a lot.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:13  SIRIMAṆḌA
text:
no speed to run away.

Make the day not-in-vain,

a little or a lot.

However much

the day passes,

that's how much less

is life.

Your last day approaches.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 6:13  SIRIMAṆḌA
text:
that's how much less

is life.

Your last day approaches.

This isn't your time

to be heedless.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 7:1  SUNDARA SAMUDDA & THE COURTESAN
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 7:1  SUNDARA SAMUDDA & THE COURTESAN

Ornamented, finely clothed,

garlanded, adorned,

her feet stained red with lac,

she wore slippers:

a courtesan.

Stepping out of her slippers—

her hands raised before me,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 7:1  SUNDARA SAMUDDA & THE COURTESAN
text:
a courtesan.

Stepping out of her slippers—

her hands raised before me,

palm-to-palm over her heart—

she softly, tenderly,

in measured words

spoke to me first:

'You are young, recluse.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 7:1  SUNDARA SAMUDDA & THE COURTESAN
text:
in measured words

spoke to me first:

'You are young, recluse.

Heed my message:

Partake of human sensuality.

I will give you luxury.

Truly I vow to you,

I will tend to you as to a fire.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 7:1  SUNDARA SAMUDDA & THE COURTESAN
text:
I will give you luxury.

Truly I vow to you,

I will tend to you as to a fire.

When we are old,

both leaning on canes,

then we will both become recluses,

winning the benefits of both worlds.'

And seeing her before me—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 7:1  SUNDARA SAMUDDA & THE COURTESAN
text:
then we will both become recluses,

winning the benefits of both worlds.'

And seeing her before me—

a courtesan, ornamented, finely clothed,

hands palm-to-palm over her heart—

like a snare of death laid out,

apt attention arose in me,

the drawbacks appeared,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 7:1  SUNDARA SAMUDDA & THE COURTESAN
text:
like a snare of death laid out,

apt attention arose in me,

the drawbacks appeared,

disenchantment stood

at an even keel:

With that, my heart was released.

See the Dhamma's true rightness!

The three knowledges

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 7:1  SUNDARA SAMUDDA & THE COURTESAN
text:
With that, my heart was released.

See the Dhamma's true rightness!

The three knowledges

have been attained;

the Buddha's bidding,

done.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA

When, knowing, 'stress, aging-&-death'—

where people run-of-the-mill are attached—

comprehending stress,

the wise man does jhāna, mindful,

there's no greater enjoyment than that.

When, striking down

attachment,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
there's no greater enjoyment than that.

When, striking down

attachment,

the bringer of stress

& craving,

the bringer of stress bound up

with objectification,

he does jhāna, mindful,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
the bringer of stress bound up

with objectification,

he does jhāna, mindful,

there's no greater enjoyment than that.

When, touching with discernment

the auspicious, two-times-four road,

the ultimate path,

cleansing away all defilement,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
the auspicious, two-times-four road,

the ultimate path,

cleansing away all defilement,

he does jhāna, mindful,

there's no greater enjoyment than that.

When he develops the peaceful state,

—sorrowless, stainless, unfabricated,

cleansing away all defilement,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
When he develops the peaceful state,

—sorrowless, stainless, unfabricated,

cleansing away all defilement,

cutting through fetters & bonds—

there's no greater enjoyment than that.

When, in the sky, the thundercloud roars,

with torrents of rain on all sides

of the path of the birds,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
When, in the sky, the thundercloud roars,

with torrents of rain on all sides

of the path of the birds,

and the monk, having gone to a cave, does jhāna,

there's no greater enjoyment than that.

When, seated on the bank of rivers

covered with flowers,

garlanded with various forest plants,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
When, seated on the bank of rivers

covered with flowers,

garlanded with various forest plants,

happy at heart, he does jhāna,

there's no greater enjoyment than that.

When, at midnight in the secluded grove,

the devas drizzle, the fanged animals roar,

and the monk, having gone to a cave, does jhāna,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
When, at midnight in the secluded grove,

the devas drizzle, the fanged animals roar,

and the monk, having gone to a cave, does jhāna,

there's no greater enjoyment than that.

When, having kept his own thoughts in check,

taking refuge in the mountains in a mountain fissure,

free from disturbance, free

from barrenness,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
taking refuge in the mountains in a mountain fissure,

free from disturbance, free

from barrenness,

he does jhāna,

there's no greater enjoyment than that.

When, happy,

destroying stain, barrenness, grief,

free from door-bolts, free from underbrush, free

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 9  BHŪTA
text:
When, happy,

destroying stain, barrenness, grief,

free from door-bolts, free from underbrush, free

from arrows,

having put an end to all effluents,

he does jhāna,

there's no greater enjoyment than that.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN

Covered in embers now are the trees,

shedding their canopy, lord, in search of fruit.

As if flaring up, they glow.

The time, great hero, partakes of savors.

The trees in bloom, delightful,

waft delights

all around, in all directions,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN
text:
The trees in bloom, delightful,

waft delights

all around, in all directions,

dropping their petals in hope of fruit.

Now, O hero, is the time to set forth.

Neither too cold nor too hot:

pleasant the season, lord, fit for a journey.

Let them see you—the Sakyans & Koliyans—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN
text:
Neither too cold nor too hot:

pleasant the season, lord, fit for a journey.

Let them see you—the Sakyans & Koliyans—

facing west, crossing in the Rohiṇī.

In hope they plow the field.

In hope the seed is sown.

In hope do merchants go to sea,

bringing back wealth.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN
text:
In hope the seed is sown.

In hope do merchants go to sea,

bringing back wealth.

Let the hope in which I stand bear fruit.

Again & again      they sow the seed.

Again & again      the deva-kings rain.

Again & again      farmers plow the fields.

Again & again      grain comes to the kingdom.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN
text:
Again & again      the deva-kings rain.

Again & again      farmers plow the fields.

Again & again      grain comes to the kingdom.

Again & again      beggars wander.

Again & again      lords of giving give.

Again & again      having given, the lords of giving

again & again      go to the heavenly place.

Truly, an enlightened one of deep discernment

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN
text:
Again & again      having given, the lords of giving

again & again      go to the heavenly place.

Truly, an enlightened one of deep discernment

cleanses, back for seven generations,

the family in which he's born.

I would imagine you to be Sakka, the deva of devas

for you engendered a sage truly named.

Suddhodana is the name of the Great Seer's father,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN
text:
I would imagine you to be Sakka, the deva of devas

for you engendered a sage truly named.

Suddhodana is the name of the Great Seer's father,

and Māyā name of the Buddha's mother

who, having nurtured the bodhisatta with her womb,

at the break-up of the body, rejoices in the threefold divine realm.

She, Gotamī, having passed away,

having fallen away from here,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN
text:
at the break-up of the body, rejoices in the threefold divine realm.

She, Gotamī, having passed away,

having fallen away from here,

is now endowed with heavenly sensual pleasures.

She rejoices in the five strings of sensuality,

surrounded by those groups of devas.

I am the son of the Buddha,

who endures what is hard to endure—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:1  KĀLUDĀYIN
text:
surrounded by those groups of devas.

I am the son of the Buddha,

who endures what is hard to endure—

Aṅgīrasa: incomparable, Such.

You, Sakka, are my father's father.

In the Dhamma, Gotama,

you are my grandfather.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'

If, in front or behind,

there is no one else,

it's extremely pleasant

for one staying alone

in the forest.

Come then! Alone

I will go to the wilderness

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
in the forest.

Come then! Alone

I will go to the wilderness

praised     by the Awakened One

pleasant     for a resolute monk

dwelling alone.

Alone,

astute in my goal,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
dwelling alone.

Alone,

astute in my goal,

I'll quickly enter the grove

—refreshing,

giving rapture

to meditators—

the haunt

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
giving rapture

to meditators—

the haunt

of elephants in rut.

When the Cool Forest's in full flower,

in a cool mountain gorge,

having bathed my limbs

I'll walk back & forth

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
in a cool mountain gorge,

having bathed my limbs

I'll walk back & forth

alone.

Ah, when will I dwell,

alone and free from companions,

in the refreshing great forest—

my task done,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
alone and free from companions,

in the refreshing great forest—

my task done,

effluent-free?

As I desire to do this,

may my purpose succeed.

I myself

will bring it about.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
may my purpose succeed.

I myself

will bring it about.

No one can do it

for anyone else.

I myself

bind on my armor.

I will enter the grove

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
I myself

bind on my armor.

I will enter the grove

and will not emerge

without having attained

the end of the effluents.

While soft breezes blow—

cool,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
the end of the effluents.

While soft breezes blow—

cool,

heavily, fragrantly scented—

I'll make ignorance burst,

as I sit on a mountaintop.

In the forest covered with blossoms

or perhaps on a cool hillside,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
as I sit on a mountaintop.

In the forest covered with blossoms

or perhaps on a cool hillside,

blessed with the bliss of release,

on Giribbaja I'll delight.

I am now he

whose resolves are fulfilled

like the moon on a full-moon night.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:2  EKAVIHĀRIYA—'DWELLING ALONE'
text:
I am now he

whose resolves are fulfilled

like the moon on a full-moon night.

With effluents all

totally ended,

there is now no further becoming.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA

Full of the many clans of impurities,

the great manufacturer of excrement,

like a stagnant pool,

a great tumor,

great wound,

full of blood & lymph,

immersed in a cesspool,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA
text:
great wound,

full of blood & lymph,

immersed in a cesspool,

trickling liquids,       the body

is oozing foulness—always.

Bound together with sixty sinews,

plastered with a stucco of muscle,

wrapped in a jacket of skin,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA
text:
Bound together with sixty sinews,

plastered with a stucco of muscle,

wrapped in a jacket of skin,

this foul body is of no worth at all.

Linked together with a chain of bones,

stitched together with tendon-threads,

it produces its various postures,

from being hitched up together.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA
text:
stitched together with tendon-threads,

it produces its various postures,

from being hitched up together.

Headed surely to death,

in the presence of the King of Mortality,

the man who learns to discard it right here,

goes wherever he wants.

Covered with ignorance,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA
text:
the man who learns to discard it right here,

goes wherever he wants.

Covered with ignorance,

the body's tied down with a four-fold tie,

sunk in the floods,

caught in the net of obsessions,

conjoined with five hindrances,

given over to thought,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA
text:
caught in the net of obsessions,

conjoined with five hindrances,

given over to thought,

accompanied with the root of craving,

roofed with delusion's roofing.

That's how the body functions,

compelled by the compulsion of kamma,

but its attainment ends

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA
text:
That's how the body functions,

compelled by the compulsion of kamma,

but its attainment ends

in ruin.

Its many becomings go

to ruin.

These who hold to this body as mine

—blind fools, people run-of-the-mill—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA
text:
to ruin.

These who hold to this body as mine

—blind fools, people run-of-the-mill—

fill the horrific cemetery,

taking on further becoming.

Those who stay uninvolved with this body

—as they would with a serpent

smeared with dung—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:5  KAPPA
text:
Those who stay uninvolved with this body

—as they would with a serpent

smeared with dung—

disgorging the root of becoming,

will, without effluent,

totally unbind.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA

You should know what's to your benefit.

You should take a good look

at the Buddha's word

& at what's fitting here

for one who has entered

on the contemplative life.

An admirable friend right here,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
for one who has entered

on the contemplative life.

An admirable friend right here,

undertaking the complete training,

& obedience to teachers:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

Respect for the Buddhas,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
This is fitting

for a contemplative.

Respect for the Buddhas,

honoring the Dhamma

as it has come to be,

& thinking highly of the Saṅgha:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
& thinking highly of the Saṅgha:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

Fitting behavior & range of association,

a livelihood purified, blameless,

the establishing of the mind:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
the establishing of the mind:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

Virtuous in what you do

& what you abstain from doing,

inspiring comportment,

commitment to the heightened mind:

This is fitting

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
inspiring comportment,

commitment to the heightened mind:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

Wilderness lodgings,

secluded, with next-to-no noise,

right for sages to resort to:

This is fitting

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
secluded, with next-to-no noise,

right for sages to resort to:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

Virtue, learning,

investigating

phenomena,

mental qualities,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
investigating

phenomena,

mental qualities,

as they have come to be:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

You should develop

inconstancy,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
for a contemplative.

You should develop

inconstancy,

the perception of not-self,

the perception of unattractiveness,

& distaste for the world:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
& distaste for the world:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

You should develop

the factors for awakening,

the bases for success,

the faculties,

& the noble eightfold path:

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
the bases for success,

the faculties,

& the noble eightfold path:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

A sage should abandon craving,

should cut through the effluents, root & all,

should dwell fully released:

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 10:7  GOTAMA
text:
A sage should abandon craving,

should cut through the effluents, root & all,

should dwell fully released:

This is fitting

for a contemplative.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 11  SAṄKICCA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 11  SAṄKICCA

What do you want in the woods, my boy,

like a bird exposed to the rain?

Monsoons refresh you,

for seclusion is for those in jhāna.

As the monsoon wind

drives the clouds in the rainy season,

so thoughts concerned with seclusion

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 11  SAṄKICCA
text:
As the monsoon wind

drives the clouds in the rainy season,

so thoughts concerned with seclusion

impel me.

A black crow

making its home in a charnel ground

inspires within me

mindfulness in—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 11  SAṄKICCA
text:
making its home in a charnel ground

inspires within me

mindfulness in—

based on dispassion for—

the body.

One whom others don't guard,

who doesn't guard others:

He is a monk

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 11  SAṄKICCA
text:
One whom others don't guard,

who doesn't guard others:

He is a monk

who lies down in ease,

unconcerned with sensual passions.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:1  SĪLAVAT
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 12:1  SĪLAVAT

Here master the virtue

that in this world is well-mastered,

for virtue, when cultivated,

brings every consummation near.

Wise, one should protect one's virtue,

aspiring to three pleasures:

praise, the gaining of wealth,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:1  SĪLAVAT
text:
Wise, one should protect one's virtue,

aspiring to three pleasures:

praise, the gaining of wealth,

and—after death—rejoicing in heaven.

The virtuous one, through restraint,

acquires many friends,

while the unvirtuous one, practicing evil,

from friends is estranged.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:1  SĪLAVAT
text:
acquires many friends,

while the unvirtuous one, practicing evil,

from friends is estranged.

The unvirtuous person gains

disrepute & dishonor;

the virtuous person, always,

repute, honor, & praise.

Virtue is the beginning, the establishing,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:1  SĪLAVAT
text:
the virtuous person, always,

repute, honor, & praise.

Virtue is the beginning, the establishing,

the mother of what is fine,

the foremost of all qualities:

Therefore virtue should be purified.

Virtue is also control, restraint,

the delight of the mind,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:1  SĪLAVAT
text:
Therefore virtue should be purified.

Virtue is also control, restraint,

Right here he gains blame,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:1  SĪLAVAT

well-concentrated on virtues.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE

Into a lowly family I was born,

poor, with next to no food.

My work was degrading:

I gathered the spoiled,

the withered flowers from shrines

and threw them away.

People found me disgusting,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
the withered flowers from shrines

and threw them away.

People found me disgusting,

despised me, disparaged me.

Lowering my heart,

I showed reverence to many.

Then I saw the One Self-awakened,

arrayed with a squadron of monks,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
I showed reverence to many.

Then I saw the One Self-awakened,

arrayed with a squadron of monks,

the Great Hero, entering the city,

supreme, of the Magadhans.

Throwing down my carrying pole,

I approached him to do reverence.

He—the supreme man—stood still

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
Throwing down my carrying pole,

I approached him to do reverence.

He—the supreme man—stood still

out of sympathy

just

for me.

After paying homage

to the feet of the teacher,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
for me.

After paying homage

to the feet of the teacher,

I stood to one side

& requested the Going Forth from him,

supreme among all living beings.

The compassionate Teacher,

sympathetic to all the world, said:

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
supreme among all living beings.

The compassionate Teacher,

sympathetic to all the world, said:

'Come, monk.'

That was my formal Acceptance.

Alone, I stayed in the wilds,

untiring,

I followed the Teacher's words,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
Alone, I stayed in the wilds,

untiring,

I followed the Teacher's words,

just as he, the Conqueror, had taught me.

In the first watch of the night,

I recollected previous lives;

in the middle watch,

purified the divine eye;

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
I recollected previous lives;

in the middle watch,

purified the divine eye;

in the last,

burst the mass of darkness.

Then, as night was ending

& the sun returning,

Indra & Brahmā came to pay homage to me,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
Then, as night was ending

& the sun returning,

Indra & Brahmā came to pay homage to me,

hands palm-to-palm at their hearts:

'Homage to you,

O thoroughbred of men,

Homage to you,

O man supreme,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
O thoroughbred of men,

Homage to you,

O man supreme,

whose effluents are ended.

You, dear sir,

are worthy of offerings.'

Seeing me,

arrayed with a squadron of devas,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 12:2  SUNĪTA THE OUTCASTE
text:
are worthy of offerings.'

Seeing me,

arrayed with a squadron of devas,

the Teacher smiled & said:

'Through austerity, celibacy,

restraint, & self-control:

That's how one is a brahman.

He is a brahman supreme.'

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA

Who once was highly exalted in the state,

having gone into the service of the king of Aṅga,

today is exalted in qualities:

Soṇa, gone beyond suffering.

Five should be cut, five abandoned,

and five above all developed.

Having gone past five bonds,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
Five should be cut, five abandoned,

and five above all developed.

Having gone past five bonds,

a monk is said to be

one who's crossed over.

For a monk who is insolent, heedless,

wishing for what's outside,

virtue, concentration, & discernment

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
For a monk who is insolent, heedless,

wishing for what's outside,

virtue, concentration, & discernment

don't go to completion,

because what should be done is cast        aside,

what shouldn't be done        is done.

For those who are insolent, heedless,

their effluents increase.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
what shouldn't be done        is done.

For those who are insolent, heedless,

their effluents increase.

But those whose mindfulness immersed in the body

is constantly well-undertaken,

—who don't engage in what shouldn't be done,

who persevere in what should be done,

mindful, alert—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
—who don't engage in what shouldn't be done,

who persevere in what should be done,

mindful, alert—

their effluents go to their end.

Go by the straight path pointed out,

don't turn back.

You yourself should reprove yourself

should advance to unbinding.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
don't turn back.

You yourself should reprove yourself

should advance to unbinding.

When I overexerted my effort,

the Teacher unexcelled in the world,

the One with Eyes,

making the lute simile,

taught me the Dhamma.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
the One with Eyes,

making the lute simile,

taught me the Dhamma.

I, having heard his words,

dwelled delighting in his bidding.

I practiced in tune,

attaining the foremost goal.

The three knowledges are attained.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
I practiced in tune,

attaining the foremost goal.

The three knowledges are attained.

The Buddha's bidding, done.

When one's awareness is dedicated

to renunciation, seclusion,

non-afflictiveness, the ending of clinging,

the ending of craving, & non-deludedness,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
to renunciation, seclusion,

non-afflictiveness, the ending of clinging,

the ending of craving, & non-deludedness,

seeing the arising of the sense media,

the mind is rightly released.

For that monk, rightly released,

his heart at peace.

There's nothing to be done,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
For that monk, rightly released,

his heart at peace.

There's nothing to be done,

nothing to add

to what's done.

As a single mass of rock isn't moved by the wind,

even so all

forms, flavors, sounds,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
As a single mass of rock isn't moved by the wind,

even so all

forms, flavors, sounds,

aromas, contacts,

ideas desirable & not,

have no effect on one who is Such.

The mind

—still, totally released—

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 13  SOṆA KOḶIVISA
text:
have no effect on one who is Such.

The mind

—still, totally released—

focuses on

their passing away.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL

Since I went forth

from home into homelessness,

I haven't known

an ignoble, aversive resolve.

'May these beings

be destroyed,

be slaughtered,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
'May these beings

be destroyed,

be slaughtered,

fall into pain'—

I've not known this resolve

in this long, long time.

But I have known goodwill,

unlimited,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
in this long, long time.

But I have known goodwill,

unlimited,

fully developed,

nurtured step after step,

as taught by the One

Awake:

to all, a friend;

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
as taught by the One

Awake:

to all, a friend;

to all, a comrade;

for all beings, sympathetic.

And I develop a mind of goodwill,

delighting in non-malevolence

—always.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
And I develop a mind of goodwill,

delighting in non-malevolence

—always.

Unvanquished, unshaken,

I gladden the mind.

I develop the sublime abiding,

not frequented by

the lowly.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
I develop the sublime abiding,

not frequented by

the lowly.

Attaining no-thinking,

the disciple of the Rightly

Self-awakened One

is endowed with noble silence

straightaway.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
Self-awakened One

is endowed with noble silence

straightaway.

As a mountain of rock

is unmoving,

firmly established,

so a monk,

with the ending of delusion,

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
firmly established,

so a monk,

with the ending of delusion,

like a mountain,

doesn't quake.

To a person without blemish,

in constant quest of what's pure,

a hair-tip of evil

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
To a person without blemish,

in constant quest of what's pure,

a hair-tip of evil

seems a storm cloud.

As a frontier fortress is guarded

within & without,

you should safeguard yourselves.

Don't let the moment

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
within & without,

you should safeguard yourselves.

Don't let the moment

pass you by.

I don't delight in death,

don't delight in living.

I await my time

like a worker his wage.

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
don't delight in living.

I await my time

like a worker his wage.

I don't delight in death,

don't delight in living.

I await my time,

mindful, alert.

The Teacher has been served by me;

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:

Attain consummation

title: THERAGĀTHĀ 14:1  REVATA'S FAREWELL
text:
the end
